mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy and suppressing equity valuations, resulting in negative forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the mean return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (HOUST) above 1.3 million units signals strong household demand and confidence, which drives corporate revenue expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where HOUST > 1.3M, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 signals weakening manufacturing activity and economic contraction, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0, or the mean return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL above 3.5% and FEDFUNDS above 1.0% signal persistent inflation and a delayed policy response, which increases real rate uncertainty and reduces equity risk appetite, leading to negative forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 1.0%, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in real personal consumption (RSAFS) above 490 billion dollars, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals strong consumer demand and confidence that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days.
regime_hint: late-cycle expansion with stable labor market
failure_condition: SPX generates negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS > 490000 and UNRATE < 4.5%, or the interaction term in a regression model is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 250k in a single month, combined with a declining unemployment rate, signals overheating labor markets that trigger inflationary expectations and preemptive Fed tightening, resulting in negative forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 250 and UNRATE < 4.2%, or the joint signal is not predictive (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% annualized, combined with rising residential investment (HOUST), signals strong economic momentum that supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX generates negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 > 2.0% and HOUST > 1.3M, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05 in regression model).
